headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 13 of the 19 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Quiet and dry weather is expected through the late week.
The extended forecast continues to be very quiet with seasonable temperatures and dry conditions prevail through next weekend.

ALY.excerpt: ) Dry weather persist across eastern New York and western New England through the upcoming week while a nor'easter develops well off shore.

GYX.excerpt: High pressure will be in control most of the upcoming week, bringing fair weather and near normal daytime temperatures.

PHI.excerpt:
The Frost Advisory is no longer in effect.
A nor'easter developing off the coast of the southern Mid- Atlantic is expected to bring coastal impacts and create hazardous marine conditions through at least the middle of this week.
A prolonged period of onshore flow will lead to multiple elevated high tide cycles this week resulting in rounds of coastal flooding.

CTP.excerpt: ) Extended stretch of dry and seasonable weather this week

RLX.excerpt: ) Strong radiational cooling amid a stagnant pattern of rather dry low/mid levels will yield more chances for frost through Thursday morning, albeit not as widespread as this morning. A Frost Advisory is in effect for locations remaining in the active growing season this morning, with additional headlines for tonight possible. Daytime highs throughout the work week will be seasonable, while overnight lows will be ~ 5 to 10 degrees below normal. Area-wide dry weather will continue through this weekend amid persistent surface high pressure.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Dry, with cold nights.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:29}} to {{t:56}}, mostly dry.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 17).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Monday 3:01 AM: "Quiet and dry weather is expected through the late week."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.
